thread:
Jordan: Heads-up: Partner is having an early baby. I'm planning to start parental leave in 2 weeks but still need to finish two interviews as part of hiring pipeline. Can I pause interviews and how do we transfer candidates? Also urgent question on PTO payout while on leave.

Tess (People Ops): First: congrats! You can pause interviewing; please mark candidates as "on hold" in Greenhouse and add a short note so hiring can reassign. If you want another interviewer to pick up, loop @Kyle to reassign panel slots. PTO payout: depends on timing; we'll confirm with Benefits.

Jordan: I'll mark Greenhouse now. If someone else steps in for interviews, what's the expected handoff doc?

Kyle (Hiring): A quick candidate summary is great: 1-2 bullet strengths, top concerns, stage-specific notes, and any outstanding take-home tasks. If scheduled loops exist, update slots and tag folks. We can send a "candidate continuity" doc template.

Marta (Benefits): PTO payout rules: if you're going on paid parental leave, you can elect to use PTO to top-up parental pay or hold PTO to return. Payout on termination only. If you want payout while on leave, we can front-load a PTO payout request but standard practice is to consume PTO during leave or keep it.

Jordan: What about performance review deadlines? My review cycle is mid-June. Will being on leave affect calibration and promotion eligibility?

Tess (People Ops): Parental leave doesn't penalize you. For performance cycles: we pause active review tasks and managers can submit a narrative from last working period. Promotions: eligibility windows may be extended—people ops will coordinate with your manager to ensure fairness.

Ibrahim (Finance): Financially, if you want to hire an interview contractor or pay an external recruiter for quick coverage, submit finance intake and include budget owner. Short contractor for interviewing is allowed for urgent roles.

Jordan: Thanks. Last Q: if I need a short unpaid extension after the paid leave, what are the steps?

Tess (People Ops): Submit an extension request in the portal at least 2w before your return date. Approvals depend on manager and People Ops. Unpaid extensions will pause employer-paid benefits after the paid leave period unless FTE remains at benefits-eligible level and you're paying your share. We'll run a benefits impact notice if you request unpaid time.

hr-bot: Helpful links: Greenhouse guidelines: https://redwood.example.company/hiring/greenhouse. Leave policy & portal: https://redwood.example.company/hr/parental-leave.

Jordan: Marked candidates and requested backup interviewers. Appreciate the support team.

Kyle (Hiring): We'll send the candidate continuity template and reassign panels. Good luck!!

(End of thread)
